html:
A wooden xylophone, or balafon, kept at Niagassola in northeastern Guinea, which tradition says belonged to Soumaoro Kante, the king of Sosso defeated by Sundiata Keita at the Battle of Kirina in the 13th century.

The Epic of Sundiata tells how the griot Bala Faseke Kouyate played it, and his descendants, the Dokala family, have guarded it ever since, playing it only on special occasions. It is held to be the ancestor of all balafons, the instrument at the heart of Mande music. UNESCO proclaimed the cultural space of the Sosso Bala a masterpiece of the intangible heritage of humanity in 2001. See also the Mande peoples.
